content.title: About
content.content: Pumpkin seeds, also called pepitas, are the edible seeds of the pumpkin (Cucurbita pepo). They have a mild nutty flavor, a crunchy texture, and are often eaten raw. Raw pepitas are nutrient‑dense and can be added to salads, smoothies, baked goods, or enjoyed as a snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pumpkin seeds have been a staple in North and Central American cuisines for centuries.
The thin hull surrounding each seed contains antioxidants such as vitamin E and carotenoids.
In some cultures they are roasted with salt and spices, while in others they are eaten raw.
Pumpkin is one of the oldest cultivated plants, grown by humans for over 7,000 years.
Seed oil is used in cosmetics and for making culinary oils.

items.title: Rich in magnesium
items.content: Magnesium supports normal muscle and nerve function and plays a role in energy metabolism.

items.title: Source of zinc
items.content: Zinc is important for immune health and skin integrity.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Vitamin E and carotenoids help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: High in plant protein
items.content: Protein from pumpkin seeds contributes to muscle maintenance and satiety.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to pumpkin seeds.

items.title: Calorie dense
items.content: Seeds are calorie‑rich, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Raw seeds contain oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pumpkin seeds can be eaten straight from the bag, tossed into salads, yogurt, oatmeal, baked goods, or blended into sauces and spreads. Soaking them for a few hours can improve digestibility.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store seeds in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer shelf life keep them in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent the oils from becoming rancid.
